1.text: Silver works as an inflation hedge when annual CPI runs above 5 percent, where it has shown a 0.
9 correlation with rising prices (Source: Gainesville Coins Historical Performance Analysis).
Below that threshold, silver behaves more like an industrial commodity than a monetary metal
so your timing and allocation size matter more than the buy itself.

2.text: You want a position built before inflation spikes, not after the headlines hit.
Most buyers either own zero silver or way too much.
A workable starting allocation for a USA retail investor is 5 percent to 10 percent of investable assets in physical precious metals
split roughly 70 percent gold and 30 percent silver.

3.text: The supply side is doing the work on its own.
The Silver Institute forecasts a sixth consecutive global silver market deficit in 2026
Six straight years of more silver leaving above-ground stocks than coming in.

4.text: Buy 10 oz bars from a known refiner.
You get more silver per dollar, and dealers will buy them back near spot.
The gold to silver ratio tells you whether silver is cheap or expensive relative to its sister metal.
You divide the gold spot price by the silver spot price.

5.text: Most USA buyers store their silver wrong.
They either hide it badly at home or pay too much for vault storage they do not need.
For positions under 200 ounces, a UL-rated home safe bolted to a concrete floor is enough.
Budget $300 to $600 for a decent unit.
